extracted.intended_audience: job applicants and aspiring publishing professionals (people exploring careers or roles at Penguin Random House)
extracted.subtask_description: A company department guide describing the responsibilities and expected outputs of each publishing department (editorial, design, production, marketing, etc.) and how they contribute to turning manuscripts into finished books and getting them to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art & Design — visual package represents book's essence and attracts target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing books is a collaborative effort. The Design staff reviews the book and meets with the Editor and Marketing department to create a visual package that will both represent the book's essence and attract the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should reflect the book's essence and be market-aware; collaboration with Editorial and Marketing is required when creating covers and visual materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio — produce high-quality audiobooks through collaboration and professional casting/recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Penguin Random House Audio works alongside dedicated Editorial, Operations, Marketing and Publicity teams to produce audiobooks across the company and beyond. The production team works with authors to cast narrators and record projects annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio production involves cross-department collaboration, narrator casting, and professional recording workflows; scale (e.g., thousands of projects/year) and quality are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts — manage and negotiate author/illustrator contracts and communicate contractual details internally
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracts department manages the process of drafting author and illustrator contracts, which covers all products for which the company acquires rights. They negotiate the fine points with the author and/or agent, and communicate with various internal departments about the details of the contract that may affect their business or authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts must clearly define rights for all product types and be negotiated with authors/agents; contract terms should be communicated to internal teams when they affect editorial, production, marketing, subsidiary rights, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Production — develop and maintain all eBook formats including fixed-layout and multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: The Digital Production team develops all eBook formats, including those with fixed layouts and those with multimedia enhancements. They collaborate with vendors, convert titles into different formats, and make corrections to existing eBook files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital production requires vendor collaboration, format conversion expertise, attention to fixed-layout/multimedia needs, and ongoing maintenance/corrections of eBook files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial — edit manuscripts for content and structure and shepherd them to finished books
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a book is acquired, an Editor works with the author to turn the manuscript into a finished book. They negotiate contracts, edit the books for content and structure, and collaborate with internal departments on how to package, market, and publicize the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial responsibilities include substantive editing (content/structure), contract negotiation, and cross-department coordination for packaging, marketing, and publicity to prepare a book for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance — manage financial aspects for books, imprints, and divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Finance is involved with everything that has a financial impact on the company, including sales forecasting, cost of goods, production, inventory, and the balance sheet for a book, imprint, or division. Finance liaises with every other department regarding corporate perspective, policies, and systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance provides forecasts, cost management, and accounting visibility; it must communicate financial constraints and metrics to editorial, production, marketing, and other teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources — support employee health, recruitment, and career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Resources partners with all divisions and departments to ensure the health and well-being of their employees through benefits administration, rewards and recognition, the facilitation of company-wide events, the recruitment of new hires, and the career development of current employees. They also act as a liaison between the employee and the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HR responsibilities include benefits, recognition programs, recruitment, events, and mediating employee-employer relationships; supports workforce capacity for publishing operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology (IT) — build and support apps, infrastructure, and networks to empower the business
rubrics_metrics.description: Penguin Random House depends on technology for virtually every aspect of the company. Our IT professionals build and support the applications, infrastructure, and networks that empower the business. We value talent who work in an agile environment and are invested in supporting a culture of entrepreneurship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT must provide reliable systems, agile development/support practices, and infrastructure that enable editorial, production, sales, and other departments to operate efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Editorial & Production Editorial — oversee in-house editorial-to-production workflow and freelancers
rubrics_metrics.description: These departments are responsible for the in-house editorial process of turning manuscripts into bound books after acquisition. This process includes maintaining and modifying the production schedules, hiring and overseeing the work of freelancers (typesetters, copy editors, proofreaders), and proofreading, and routing jackets and manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management must maintain production schedules, coordinate and supervise freelance vendors (typesetters, copy editors, proofreaders), perform proofreading, and ensure correct routing of materials to meet manufacturing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing — develop and implement creative, market-informed campaigns to promote books
rubrics_metrics.description: The Marketing department develops and implements creative campaigns, including advertising, social media, and bookstore displays. Marketers work closely with Sales to learn about the market to promote books and writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing should create audience-targeted, creative promotional plans and coordinate with Sales for market insights; channels include advertising, social media, and in-store merchandising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production — oversee pre-press and manufacturing to produce books on-time and on-budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The Production department oversees the pre-press and manufacturing process from manuscript to bound book. The team works with outside printers, book manufacturers, and other vendors to produce our books within the desired timeframe and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production must manage vendor relationships, quality control, schedules, and budgets to ensure finished books meet specifications and delivery timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity — generate exposure and secure media coverage and events to create buzz
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity professionals generate exposure and 'buzz' for new books. Publicists pitch to newspapers, television, radio stations, websites, and bloggers to review our titles and feature stories about forthcoming books and authors. Publicists also help create social media outreach, author tours, author signings, readings, and other events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity work includes media pitching, organizing author events/tours/signings, and activating social outreach to generate coverage and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing Operations — secure materials, manage vendors, and forecast inventory to ensure quality and on-schedule production
rubrics_metrics.description: The groups within Publishing Operations secure raw materials for printing traditional books, manage relationships with key vendors to ensure that our books are high quality and produced on schedule, and forecast inventory levels to determine when books need reprinting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations must ensure supply chain reliability (materials, vendors), quality control in manufacturing, and accurate inventory forecasting for reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales — place and merchandise books so they are available and discoverable to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sales team works with booksellers, teachers, and librarians so that our books are available to readers in brick and mortar shops, online retailers, schools, and libraries. Sales teams also ensure that our books are well displayed, merchandised, and promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sales responsibilities include retail/educational outreach, placement strategies, in-store/display merchandising, and coordination with Marketing to drive discoverability and purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary Rights — license derivative and territorial rights to maximize revenue and opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Subsidiary Rights departments for each of our publishing divisions handle the licensing of any rights of the original book in both domestic and foreign markets. Translations, magazine excerpts, audio editions, and book club inclusions are some examples of subrights. Their primary responsibility is to negotiate contracts with licensees to maximize revenue and publishing opportunities for the author and the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsidiary rights teams identify licensing opportunities (translations, excerpts, audio, book clubs), negotiate contracts, and manage territory/format rights to optimize revenue and author exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warehouse / Distribution — receive, store, pick, pack, and ship books efficiently at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Penguin Random House is the premier provider of distribution services in the publishing industry. Our state-of-the-art national fulfillment centers receive, store, pick, pack, and ship out on average more than 1.8 million books daily to customers worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution operations must maintain high-throughput, accurate fulfillment, inventory handling, and shipping processes to meet customer demand and support sales channels.
